newsitem.title: USA: CFM Technologies Q2 orders trail Q1's.
newsitem.headline: CFM Technologies Q2 orders trail Q1's.

text.p: CFM Technologies Inc said Thursday that no orders for flat panel displays (FPDs) were received during its second quarter, and total orders for the period trailed the first quarter's.

Customer orders for the second quarter of fiscal 1997 were $12.2 million, contributing to orders for the first half of 1997 of $41.9 million. Backlog at quarter-end stood at $25.3 million. FPD systems represented 64 percent of the backlog.
"While total quarterly orders represent a decline from those reported in the first quarter, we anticipate continued growth in demand for our products," said chief executive officer Roger Carolin.
Flat panel displays are thin display screens used in portable computers.
CFM shares were down 8-3/8 in mid-morning at 29.
The company said significant improvements in manufacturing productivity offset aggressive pricing decisions it made as part of its market penetration strategy.
CFM said such pricing will continue to impact gross margins for the remainder of this fiscal year.
Gross margin for the second quarter of 1997 ended April 30 was 46.5 percent compared with 49.6 percent in the second quarter of 1996 and 46.1 percent in the first quarter of 1997.

The company said it anticipates further increases in spending in support of research, development and engineering as new, larger FPD platforms are introduced, 300mm semiconductor platform development continues, and new processes are developed for existing and new equipment.

"The FPD industry is experiencing very rapid growth and product mix changes which, in turn, require rapid new product development by equipment suppliers," said chairman Chris McConnell. "We are meeting these challenges in developing new generation FPD products and believe that this experience will, in turn, benefit our 300mm semiconductor and subsequent generation FPD system development efforts."

CFM Thursday reported second quarter net sales rose to $20.1 million from $10.1 million in the second quarter of 1996. Net income in the '97 first quarter was $1,980,000 or $0.25 per share, on 7,964,000 weighted average common shares outstanding, versus $625,000 or $0.16 per share on 3,994,000 shares.
